title: PhantyQuad [Blender Plugin]
author: Rizzlord
selftext:
Hey, i was very annoyed, that all the AI 3d models had bad topology, so i made a quad remesher Plugin for blender. For now its Linux Only, but it will soon have windows.

  
Would be a shame if this goes against TOS :D

comments.author: GigaTerra
comments.body: Yea, no you have been out marketed by Quad Remesher. Sure yours is cheaper but the results look similar to the build in remesher Blender has, that is based on the free Github one.

replies.author: Rizzlord
replies.body:
Yeah way cheaper, commercial licence for quad remesher is 100$. 

Also you can try to use any of the free remeshing tools, they either break or have holes, even on a high quad level. 

And most of the time you cant remesh at all because most AI generated models are not watertight, with my tool it does not matter, its perfect for locally generated 3d AI models.

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body:
I think you are using the free versions of AI 3D model tools, because the payed services export manifold meshes, and even allows you to explode them into manifold pieces.

While yours is cheaper your quality is an fraction of what Quad Remesher provides, similar to what the build in remesher in Blender does. Not to mention there are multiple free topology tools on GitHub right now that out performs Blender's default one.

It would make more sense for people to spend the money on 3D AI, to get the better quality generation, than to use your tool.

replies.author: Rizzlord
replies.body: Yes I generate models locally. You don't have to buy it, and that is your option. But the reality is a very different topic if you work everyday with free quad remesh tools like the ones in blender.

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body:
Even in that case there are easy work around in Blender. Blender has an 3D printing plugin that can help find and plug holes. Not to mention Blender has an Voxel remesh option that can be used to make an mesh manifold. From there the user just has to re-bake textures. Lastly custom retopolgy will always give better results than any of the current tools.

And an tip from someone who uses these tools all the time, you can do small details like wires and other small details, by using an 3D cube as an place holder, and then scaling the details larger. I then scale them down and merge them with the mesh. I always wonder why no one making these tools build that type of thing into the code.

replies.author: Rizzlord
replies.body: I like how you just proved my point and the usability of my tool while trying to redundan it. As you said, you have to do workarounds here and there and many manual steps, which i want to avoid and just quick and nice have a good mesh. Thank you for that.

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body: No those methods gives better results than your tool. You understand 3D modelers don't want skewed topology. Your quality is on par with free tools, as in there is no reason to buy yours. Because people would rather pay for better AI, or better topology tools, than pay for quality they can get for free.

replies.author: Rizzlord
replies.body: Makes no sense taking to someone who didn't get what the tool is for. If you think "I don't need that" then you are not the target audience. Simple as that. Thank you for the unnecessary discussion.

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body:
>Then you are not the target audience. 

Then I am not, and that is kind of funny as I am the type of person who buys these tools and look for these tools. But you are right, I I prefer my tool creators care about topology as much as I do.

I wish you luck.
